Analysis: Hypothesis 1 introduces additional mechanistic layers by integrating IL-6–STAT3 signaling with CAF-induced ECM stiffening and YAP/TAZ-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. This added complexity is novel and could potentially elucidate deeper interactions in cholangiocarcinoma, but it raises issues regarding mechanistic clarity and sequential interdependence, which compromises its plausibility and testability. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 is more focused, linking CAF-induced ECM stiffening directly to YAP/TAZ activation and subsequent epigenetic modifications. Its streamlined nature enhances its plausibility and testability, even though it is somewhat less novel by not addressing inflammatory signaling. Both hypotheses appear safe in the context of experimental models, but Hypothesis 2 is superior overall because its simplicity improves the likelihood of rigorous experimental validation without sacrificing key mechanistic insight.
